title: Singapore weekly: BTO applications close; December referral terms need a separate check
summary: 9–15 November: the BTO window ended and reviewed SC referral terms point to December eligibility changes. Existing quarterly rates and bank illustrations remain context, not new offers.

takeaways.text: The November BTO application window ended on 11 November.
SC's revised referral period is 4–31 December, with Letter of Offer acceptance due by 15 January.
No current SORA fixing or new fully verified mortgage promotion was established in this review.

sections.heading: The week's housing deadline
sections.text: HDB's November BTO administrative annex specifies applications from 4 to 11 November 2026, requiring a valid HFE letter. It describes computer-ballot shortlisting, not first-come priority. The application window has therefore ended; this review does not establish final application totals or ballot results.

sections.heading: Referral terms reviewed during the week
sections.text: SC's amendment was first covered by RatePro on 11 November; neither bank document states its publication date, so this is not described as a new announcement that day. Changes take effect on 4 December. Referred applicants and co-applicants must be at least 21, have no active mortgage account with SC and meet the preceding-12-month loan-redemption restriction. Clause 13 allows reward refusal or recovery for misconduct, breaches and other stated conditions.

sections.heading: Two separate referral deadlines
sections.text: The revised PDF specifies a 4–31 December promotion period. A successful referral requires bank approval and Letter of Offer acceptance by 15 January 2027. Eligible existing personal-banking customers receive the referral fee; consent and disclosure requirements apply, and staff and bridging loans are excluded. This is a referrer arrangement, not a verified borrower subsidy or mortgage-rate offer.

sections.heading: Older macro context, not weekly changes
sections.text: MAS's October summary says it kept the Singapore dollar on its existing appreciating path. CPF still lists OA interest of 2.50% and HDB mortgage interest of 2.60% p.a. for 1 October–31 December. SingStat's 23 October entries report Q3 private residential prices up 1.4% and HDB resale prices down 0.1% quarter-on-quarter. These reference periods precede this reporting week.

sections.heading: Bank comparison context
sections.text: UOB's indicative completed-property schedule remains 3M compounded SORA plus 0.70% in years 1–2, 0.80% in year 3 and 1.00% thereafter: two-year lock-in, minimum SGD250,000, limited tranche for new direct-to-bank customers purchasing or refinancing. Its Letter of Offer confirms rates and benefits. Maximum loan, full charges, subsidy recovery and availability deadline are not established here. DBS's rewards page states a 31 December deadline, but complete qualifying and clawback terms remain unverified; no confirmed promotion record is added.

sections.heading: What readers should do with this evidence
sections.text: Compare the entire rate schedule, benchmark tenor, reset dates, loan/property eligibility, lock-in and exit costs before valuing a reward. The MAS statistics read returned an invalid-period message, so this review supplies no fixing or funding-cost trend. CPF's historical deposit input is not a current marginal bank-funding measure. A US rate move or MAS exchange-rate stance does not establish an immediate matching change in a Singapore mortgage. Referral eligibility does not establish loan approval.

sections.heading: Coverage and dates
sections.text: This retrospective covers 9–15 November in Asia/Singapore and was written on 16 November. Its end date is a reporting boundary, not an offer expiry. Source checks below record actual UTC reads. HDB's annex states no publication date; SC's publication dates are unknown. The CPF source update date is retained separately from its quarter. This weekly synthesis does not renew earlier observations or claim collector recovery.
